# Entry-cadence study: weekly vs daily vs breakout-confirmed daily
**HISTORICAL BACKTEST — hypothetical, not forward evidence.** Script `run_cadence_study.py`, output `validation/cadence_study.json` (generated by running it against the cached 7-year yfinance daily data of the current S&P 500 + Nasdaq-100 members, 2021-01-04 → 2026-10; live defaults, nothing tuned).

**Pre-declared rule (written into the script before the run):** adopt daily (or breakout-daily) as default only if ALL hold: OOS trades ≥ 30; OOS **and** IS net return (MYR, after exit FX) ≥ weekly; OOS Sharpe ≥ weekly; OOS max drawdown not worse than weekly by > 3 pp; still ≥ weekly under 2× costs. Split fixed in advance: dev/IS 2021-2023, test/OOS 2024-.

| Arm | IS trades | IS net ret | OOS trades | OOS net ret | OOS max DD | OOS Sharpe | OOS costs (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| weekly (default) | 65 | +27.4 % | 94 | +25.1 % | −7.9 % | 0.99 | 43 |
| daily | 82 | +36.1 % | 111 | +26.2 % | −10.5 % | 0.87 | 53 |
| breakout_daily | 72 | +42.6 % | 98 | +2.1 % | −9.1 % | 0.26 | 40 |

Cost sensitivity (OOS net return, ×1 / ×2 / ×3 modelled spread+slippage): weekly 25.1 / 23.6 / 20.1; daily 26.2 / 23.9 / 28.5 (non-monotonic = noise); breakout 2.1 / 0.8 / 0.2.
Parameter stability (±1 step, IS/OOS): daily OOS swings from +2.2 % (ATR stop +0.5) to +29.8 % (score −5); weekly OOS stays +14.7 % … +25.1 %. Yearly regimes: daily better in 2021, worse in 2022/2023/2025; no arm is consistently ahead.
**Decision (by the rule): daily FAILS** (OOS Sharpe 0.87 < 0.99; all other checks passed) and breakout_daily fails 3 checks → **weekly stays the default; `entry_cadence` is an owner setting** (`weekly|daily|breakout_daily`). Daily produces ~18 % more trades, ~23 % higher costs, and a deeper drawdown for statistically indistinguishable return: the evidence is **not credible enough** to adopt it. Cash remains a valid decision in every arm.

**Read this plainly:** over the same OOS window buy-and-hold total return was **SPY +70.1 %, QQQ +89.3 %** (USD, adjusted close incl. dividends) versus swing +25 % (MYR, after costs and exit FX) with ≤ 80 % exposure — the strategy lagged both benchmarks in this backtest, in a strongly rising market. The universe is today's index members (survivorship bias; see VALIDATION.md), which makes the strategy's number *optimistic*, not pessimistic.
